answer: Each applicant files one reef sheet for the atlas and locks a 70-credit bond. The sheet states its reef area and carries a lantern seal key-bound to coordinates. An auditor recomputes it against the atlas grid; overstating it over 5 percent, copying a sector, or reusing a lantern seal burns the bond. First costs 26; kth costs 26+6(k-1), so 1000th costs 6020 and 1000 fakes pay 3,023,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-atlas ring fails: its sheet shares seal and coordinates with the original reef filing. An honest surveyor files once, pays 26, and recovers it after audit.
